title: Delta Lake, partitioning and the file layout that defines the bill

videos.script: A Delta table never edits a file it has written. {{never}} Every change writes new files, and one line in a log that adds them and removes the old ones. In this lesson you delete one order, and watch a whole month get copied to do it. {{delete}} Then the same October is written four ways. You ask each one the same two questions, and count the bytes it reads. {{layouts}} A partition by day cuts a day's question to a fifth. So do the statistics in the log, with no partitions at all. {{skip}} A table loaded every hour becomes hundreds of small files. Compaction makes them one a day again. {{compact}} And every old version stays on disk, which is how you travel back in time. {{travel}} Vacuum is the one command that deletes it. After it, the log still describes the past, and the files are gone. {{vacuum}} Everything runs on your laptop, with no emulator. A Delta table is the same folder on a disk as in OneLake. {{laptop}}
